question: A 6-year-old boy with moderate Intellectual Disability Disorder (IQ 42, confirmed adaptive deficits) presents to your clinic. His parents want to know what should be done first. He has no psychiatric comorbidities, no seizures, and his hearing and vision tests are normal. Which of the following is the highest-priority initial management step?

answers.text: Prescribe a trial of donepezil to improve memory and cognitive function

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Donepezil (an acetylcholinesterase inhibitor) is used in Alzheimer's dementia, not IDD. No medication currently reverses or meaningfully improves the intellectual deficit in IDD.

answers.text: Refer to a special education programme and initiate speech-language therapy

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. The cornerstone of IDD management is habilitation — structured special education and allied health therapies (speech-language, occupational, physiotherapy as appropriate). These interventions maximise adaptive functioning and independence, which is the primary treatment goal.

answers.text: Admit to a residential psychiatric facility for behavioural observation

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Residential admission is not indicated in the absence of psychiatric comorbidity, severe self-harm, or unsafe home circumstances. Community-based habilitation is strongly preferred.

answers.text: Order chromosomal microarray to identify the genetic cause before beginning any intervention

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. While aetiological investigation is important, it should not delay the start of habilitation. Therapy begins as soon as the diagnosis is established; genetic workup proceeds in parallel, not as a prerequisite.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the IDD management framework: (1) habilitation — special education + allied therapies; (2) treat psychiatric comorbidities pharmacologically if present; (3) family psychoeducation and support; (4) preventive healthcare. Pharmacotherapy for the intellectual deficit itself has no role.

Correct reasoning. Management of IDD is habilitation-first: special education + allied therapies to maximise adaptive function. No medication reverses the underlying deficit. Aetiological workup proceeds in parallel, never as a gate to therapy.
